countries.name: Alaska
countries.subtitle: Glaciers, whales and bears, by small ship
countries.leading: Alaska is the largest wild coast the house sells: tidewater glaciers, fjords and island channels where humpback whales feed all summer, and a peninsula of volcanoes and brown bears that runs out into the Aleutian chain. About 60 percent of all the land the National Park Service manages is here. The house sends you by small ship, with UnCruise Adventures, from Juneau, Sitka, Ketchikan and Seward, and plans the bear coast, the national parks and the northern lights around the voyage.

story.eyebrow: Glaciers, whales and bears, by small ship
story.title: The Wild Coast of North America

blocks.p: Alaska holds 15 national parks, preserves, monuments and historical parks, and the National Park Service says about 60 percent of all the land it manages is in the state, most of it set aside by the Alaska National Interest Lands Conservation Act of 1980. The season for the coast is short and bright: Glacier Bay's main visitor season runs from late May to early September, peaking in July, and no roads lead into the park, so it is reached by air or by water. That is why the house plans Alaska around small ships. A yacht of 22 to 88 guests reaches the coves, glacier faces and island passages that large ships cannot, with kayaks and skiffs launched from the stern.

blocks.h: Humpback whales, Glacier Bay and Icy Strait
blocks.p: Humpbacks use Glacier Bay as spring, summer and fall feeding habitat. The National Park Service documented 158 individual humpbacks in Glacier Bay and Icy Strait between 1 June and 31 August 2025, and most winter in Hawaiʻi, with at least 10 percent going to Mexico. UnCruise's Glacier Wilderness week from Juneau sails Icy Strait, and Frederick Sound off Admiralty Island adds killer, minke and fin whales.

At Brooks Camp in Katmai National Park, bears arrive with the salmon in late June. Mid July usually brings the largest number of bears to the river, and the dominant bears fish at Brooks Falls itself. Most leave in August, then return from late August, and September usually has high numbers again, fishing the lower river. The Aleutian Islands Adventure lands on the Katmai coast; Brooks Camp itself is reached by floatplane, which the house adds on, with time to spare for weather.

Kenai Fjords National Park, created in 1980, covers more than 600,000 acres beside Seward. The Harding Icefield, over 700 square miles, feeds about 40 tidewater glaciers, and the water holds humpback whales, orcas, Dall's porpoises, harbor seals, Steller sea lions and sea otters, with tufted and horned puffins among more than 190 bird species. The best months are May to September.

Denali's large animals are the moose, grizzly bear, caribou, Dall sheep and grey wolf, across open tundra below North America's highest peak. UnCruise's National Parks by Land and Sea pairs Denali with a week at sea.

Explore Fairbanks dates the aurora season from 21 August to 21 April. On a clear, dark night the lights are visible an average of four nights in five, and three nights or more, out late in the evening, raises the odds above 90 percent. A late August or September voyage can end in Fairbanks for both.

May: the first sailings, snow on the peaks, humpbacks returning. June: long light, bears on the Katmai coast, the Aleutian sailings begin. July: the height of the season, the most bears at Brooks Falls, whales in Glacier Bay. August: salmon in the streams, the last Aleutian sailings, aurora season opens on 21 August. September: bears back on the rivers, the last Inside Passage weeks, northern lights in the interior.
Every UnCruise ship, route and 2027 and 2028 sailing is filed under Alaska voyages; the Aleutians and a whole Safari Quest charter are in Terra Y.

image.alt: Alaska: The Best Wildlife Viewing in Alaska

facts: Best months
Late May to early September for the coast, peaking in July; July and September for Katmai's bears; from 21 August for the northern lights in Fairbanks.
Getting there

Fly to Juneau, Sitka, Ketchikan or Anchorage (for Seward). Glacier Bay has no road in: it is reached by air or by water. UnCruise includes the airport transfers on embarkation and disembarkation days.
Who it suits
Couples, families and friends who want wildlife at close range and the coast by small ship, from a whole yacht for one party to a week of kayaks and skiffs.
Signature experiences

Humpbacks in Icy Strait and Glacier Bay, kayaking to tidewater glaciers, brown bears on the Katmai coast, Kenai Fjords' sea otters and puffins, the Aleutian chain to Dutch Harbor, and the northern lights from Fairbanks.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Alaska?
faqs.a: For the coast, late May to early September. Glacier Bay's main season runs from late May to early September, peaking in July, and UnCruise sails from May to September. For bears at Brooks Falls, July and September; for the northern lights, the aurora season in Fairbanks runs from 21 August to 21 April.

faqs.q: Where is the best wildlife viewing in Alaska?
faqs.a: Glacier Bay and Icy Strait for humpback whales (158 individuals documented in summer 2025), Katmai for brown bears, Kenai Fjords for orcas, sea otters, Steller sea lions and puffins, and Denali for moose, grizzlies, caribou, Dall sheep and wolves.

faqs.q: When can you see bears fishing at Brooks Falls?
faqs.a: The National Park Service says bears arrive with the salmon in late June, are most numerous in mid July, mostly leave in August, and return in high numbers in September, when most fish the lower Brooks River.

faqs.q: When are humpback whales in Southeast Alaska?
faqs.a: Humpbacks feed in Glacier Bay through spring, summer and fall. The Park Service's core count runs from 1 June to 31 August; most of the whales winter in Hawaiʻi and at least 10 percent in Mexico.

faqs.q: Why see Alaska by small ship?
faqs.a: No roads reach Glacier Bay, and much of the coast is reached only by water. UnCruise's yachts carry 22 to 88 guests and launch kayaks and skiffs from the stern, so the day goes into coves, glacier faces and island channels rather than ports.

faqs.q: Can you see the northern lights on an Alaska trip?
faqs.a: Yes, from late August. Explore Fairbanks dates the aurora season from 21 August to 21 April, with the lights visible on average four clear, dark nights in five. A late summer voyage can end with nights in Fairbanks.

countries.name: Argentina
countries.subtitle: Where Wilderness Meets Soul
countries.leading: From blue-ice glaciers and wind-swept pampas to vineyard-draped foothills and thunderous waterfalls, Argentina is a country of grand contrasts. Carefully crafted journeys here trade generic sightseeing for layered, local access that reveals both wild places and the human stories that shape them.

story.title: A Land of Glaciers, Plains, and Powerful Contrast

blocks.p: Argentina unfolds across dramatic, clearly defined landscapes: the blue ice of Los Glaciares National Park, the endless grass of the pampas, the jagged skyline of Fitz Roy, and the lush roar of Iguazú. The scale of the country makes travel here an exercise in contrast, where a single journey can move from alpine silence to metropolitan energy.

Journeys that matter are planned to respect those contrasts, with time carved out to walk under glaciers, ride with gauchos on working estancias, and linger at table in a bodega. Our approach links privileged access, local specialists, and slower pacing so the places you visit stop feeling like boxes on a list and start feeling like parts of a story.

Plan your Argentina trip with Wild & Co. Safaris and expect itineraries tuned to rhythm and detail: private guides for hiking in Patagonia, curated tastings in Mendoza, and entry to viewpoints and encounters that shift a visit into a lasting memory.

image.alt: Argentina: A Land of Glaciers, Plains, and Powerful Contrast

story.title: Where Nature, Culture, and Energy Align

blocks.p: Hike in Los Glaciares to stand on the fronts of living ice, follow trails beneath Fitz Roy, or search for marine mammals off Peninsula Valdés. These are active, place-focused experiences that reward early starts and quiet attention.

Buenos Aires is a counterpoint to the wild: intimate parrillas, late-night music, and neighbourhoods that reveal the country’s immigrant and artistic threads. Time in the city is curated around private studio visits, culinary access, and performances that feel local rather than touristy.

A stay at a working estancia reframes the pampas as a place of skill and tradition, not an exhibit: riding with gauchos, learning equitation, and sharing meals under open skies connect you to Argentina’s rural heart.

In Mendoza and the high-altitude valleys, tastings are paired with vineyard walks and conversations about altitude viticulture. Meals are moments of cultural exchange, where ingredient provenance and craft matter as much as the bottle.

Journeys are assembled from region-specific specialists: local guides, small family-run lodges, and private transfers that eliminate waiting and add depth. The result is not a packaged tour, it is a crafted passage through landscapes and communities that reveal Argentina at its most authentic.

image.alt: Argentina: Where Nature, Culture, and Energy Align

facts: Best months
October to April for general travel, November to March for Patagonia, March to April for Mendoza’s grape harvest and milder autumn weather.
Getting there

Most international flights arrive into Buenos Aires Ezeiza (EZE), with efficient domestic connections to regional airports such as El Calafate (for southern Patagonia), Ushuaia, Mendoza, and Puerto Iguazú; many journeys combine short internal flights with private transfers.
Who it suits

Travelers who want bold natural scenery paired with cultural depth: couples seeking intimate, romantic moments, families comfortable with active days, adventure travelers, solo explorers, photographic specialists, and luxury travellers seeking private-guided, service-led experiences.
Signature experiences

Glacier treks and viewpoints in Los Glaciares, guided hikes beneath Fitz Roy, estancia riding on the pampas, curated tastings in Mendoza, waterfall vistas at Iguazú, and marine-wildlife encounters at Peninsula Valdés, all accessed through private guides and locally rooted lodges.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Argentina?
faqs.a: Timing depends on region: October to April covers spring and summer across most of the country, with Patagonia at its best from November to March and Mendoza particularly inviting during the grape harvest in March and April. Iguazú is visitable year-round, though water flow and humidity vary seasonally.

faqs.q: Is Argentina safe for travelers?
faqs.a: Argentina is generally safe for visitors who take normal urban precautions, such as guarding belongings in city centres and avoiding unattended areas after dark. Political demonstrations can occur in major cities, so check local advice and follow guidance from your accommodation and guides.

faqs.q: How many days do you need in Argentina?
faqs.a: For a meaningful multi-region trip allow 10 to 14 days to combine Patagonia, Buenos Aires, and a region like Mendoza or Iguazú; a focused trip to one area works in 6 to 8 days. Internal flights reduce transit time but plan for full travel days between distant regions.

faqs.q: What is Argentina famous for?
faqs.a: Argentina is known for its glaciers and mountain scenery in Patagonia, the sheer power of Iguazú Falls, the cultural life of Buenos Aires with tango and gastronomy, world-class Malbec from Mendoza, and vast pampas where gaucho traditions remain alive.

faqs.q: What are the signature land experiences and how long should I spend on them?
faqs.a: Signature experiences include trekking and glacier viewpoints in Los Glaciares National Park, estancia stays and riding in the pampas, wine tastings and vineyard visits in Mendoza, and wildlife viewing at Peninsula Valdés. Plan 4 to 7 days for Patagonia, 2 to 3 days for Mendoza, 1 to 2 days for Iguazú, and 2 to 3 days for Valdés to experience each region properly.

faqs.q: Does Argentina offer cruises or water-based excursions?
faqs.a: Argentina has boat-based excursions such as glacier-front and riverboat viewpoints near Perito Moreno and Iguazú, plus seasonal whale-watching off Peninsula Valdés, but My Epic Africa does not offer cruise-style itineraries in Argentina and focuses on land-based, privately guided journeys.

countries.name: Arizona
countries.subtitle: Why Journey To Arizona
countries.leading: Warm desert light sculpts red rock amphitheaters, saguaro-studded valleys, and vast skies that feel endless. Arizona is a landscape of layered stone and quiet scale, where carefully crafted journeys reveal hidden canyons, night skies, and the rhythms of the desert.

story.title: A Land of Canyons, Color, and Timeless Landscapes

blocks.p: Arizona is a place where the earth writes its history in strata of color, sweeping plateaus, and carved canyons. From the rim of the Grand Canyon to the red rock mesas of Sedona and the saguaros of the Sonoran Desert, each place offers a distinct mood and light that changes through the day.

Travel in Arizona with Wild & Co. Safaris is about composition and pace: private-guided hikes at dawn, secluded ranch stays, and evenings beneath sky so full of stars they feel tangible. Our journeys prioritize local access and conservation-minded partners, so you experience iconic overlooks and quieter, less-visited corridors that reveal the state beyond postcards.

image.alt: Arizona: A Land of Canyons, Color, and Timeless Landscapes

story.title: Where Canyons, Culture & Desert Light Align

blocks.p: Nature lovers drawn to stark desert beauty, photographers chasing ephemeral light, couples seeking intimate desert retreats, families interested in outdoor adventure and cultural learning, and solo travelers after safe, private-guided exploration all find thoughtful options here.

Walk the rim of the Grand Canyon at sunrise, wander red rock trails around Sedona, explore slot canyons near Page, or cross high ponderosa forests and alpine meadows in northern Arizona. Each region presents its own geology and microclimate, offering varied terrain within a single state.

Accommodations range from remote luxury ranches and boutique desert lodges to private houses and thoughtfully placed glamping tents, each chosen for their relationship to the landscape and service that supports bespoke itineraries.

Guided hikes, horseback rides, jeep outings, birding and botany walks, and curated cultural visits to Indigenous communities and small towns form the backbone of our itineraries. We design routes to balance iconic highlights with quieter moments of solitude and observation.
Plan for seasonal light and weather: cool mornings, expansive afternoons, and extraordinary night skies. Time in Arizona is measured in vistas and silence as much as in miles traveled.

image.alt: Arizona: Where Canyons, Culture & Desert Light Align

facts: Best months
March to May and September to November for mild temperatures and clear light; winter is pleasant in lower deserts while summer is hot with a brief monsoon season in July and August.
Getting there

Major gateways are Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport and Tucson International Airport, with Flagstaff and Page regional airports for northern access; a vehicle or private transfer is essential to reach remote lodges and trailheads, and private charters are available for bespoke itineraries.
Who it suits

Desert and nature lovers, photographers, couples seeking intimate escapes, families looking for outdoor learning, active travelers wanting guided hikes and horseback adventures, and luxury travelers seeking private, service-led stays.
Signature experiences

Grand Canyon rim and sunrise walks, Sedona red rock hikes and photographic light, slot canyon exploration near Page, Sonoran Desert saguaro valleys and birding, stargazing under minimal light pollution, and curated cultural visits to Indigenous communities and historic frontier towns.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Arizona?
faqs.a: Spring and fall, roughly March through May and September through November, offer the most comfortable daytime temperatures and clear light; summer brings monsoon storms in the south and hot desert temperatures, while winter is mild in low deserts and snowy at higher elevations.

faqs.q: Is Arizona safe for travelers?
faqs.a: Yes, Arizona is generally safe for travelers who use normal precautions: stay hydrated, plan for remote travel times, tell someone your route in backcountry areas, and respect local regulations and Indigenous lands.

faqs.q: How many days do you need in Arizona?
faqs.a: A focused 5 to 7 days lets you explore one or two regions in depth, while 10 to 14 days allows a curated route that links the Grand Canyon, Sedona, and the Sonoran Desert with time for guided outings and rest.

faqs.q: What is Arizona famous for?
faqs.a: Arizona is best known for the Grand Canyon, the red rock formations around Sedona, the iconic saguaro-studded Sonoran Desert, dramatic slot canyons near Page, and rich Native American cultural traditions.

faqs.q: What are Arizona's signature land experiences and where should I stay?
faqs.a: Signature experiences include sunrise or rim walks at the Grand Canyon, red rock hikes and vortex viewpoints in Sedona, guided slot canyon visits near Page, and desert ecology and birding in the Sonoran Desert. Stay in remote lodges, boutique desert resorts, or private ranch houses chosen for access to these landscapes and for privacy.

faqs.q: Are guided walking or trekking options available?
faqs.a: Yes, experienced local guides lead half-day to multi-day hikes, rim-to-river or canyon-floor walks where permitted, interpretive desert botany walks, and horseback outings; some areas on tribal land require guided access or permits.

countries.name: Australia
countries.subtitle: Why Journey To Australia
countries.leading: From red deserts and sculpted gorges to coral gardens and eucalyptus‑fringed coastlines, Australia is a continent of singular ecosystems and scale. Carefully crafted journeys here trade crowds for remote access, local expertise, and deep encounters with places that feel both ancient and elemental.

story.title: A Continent of Vast Landscapes and Living Nature

blocks.p: Australia’s scale is the first thing you notice: wide, open deserts that hold millennia of stories, lush rainforests that hum with life, and coasts where coral reefs and kelp forests meet the horizon. Each region has its own tempo and ecology, and thoughtfully designed travel lets you move between them with purpose, rather than treat them as postcard stops.

Journeys by Wild & Co. Safaris focus on access and depth: private guides who understand seasonal windows, curated stays that place you inside landscapes rather than outside them, and experiences timed for wildlife and light. The result is not a checklist itinerary, it is a series of encounters shaped around where nature is most alive and where the continent’s contrasts are most meaningful.

image.alt: Australia: A Continent of Vast Landscapes and Living Nature

story.title: Where Nature, Wildlife, and Adventure Connect

blocks.p: Explore crystalline reefs, secluded bays, and coastal trails by private boat, dive, or guided snorkel; the Great Barrier Reef and Ningaloo are living laboratories for marine life and offer tailored experiences from day trips to liveaboard expeditions.

Traverse ochre plains, hidden waterholes, and ancient rock art with local guides who unlock stories of country and culture; remote, small-group or private journeys focus on slow exploration, night skies, and encounters with unique flora and fauna.

Walk under canopy, search for tree-dwelling mammals and rare birds, or island-hop to discover pristine beaches and endemic species; Tasmania, the Daintree, and offshore islands each offer concentrated wilderness in compact, accessible forms.

For dramatic tides, sandstone gorges, and coastal wildlife, small-ship expeditions and bespoke charters provide the access and expertise to explore marine‑and‑land interface zones that are otherwise unreachable by road.

image.alt: Australia: Where Nature, Wildlife, and Adventure Connect

facts: Best months

September to November and March to May provide broadly mild weather and lower crowds for much of the country; the northern wet season runs roughly November to April, making the dry winter months preferable for tropical regions and Kimberley expeditions.
Getting there

Major international gateways are Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Perth, and Darwin, with frequent domestic flights connecting to regional hubs and remote airstrips; many remote lodges and expeditions require domestic flights or private charters to reach.
Who it suits

Travelers who seek dramatic natural diversity, from luxury seekers and honeymooners to families, solo adventurers, and specialist wildlife photographers; Australia supports bespoke, active, and conservation-minded itineraries across varied terrains.
Signature experiences

Diving or snorkeling the Great Barrier Reef and Ningaloo Reef, guided exploration of the Red Centre and its rock art, small-ship Kimberley expeditions, wildlife encounters on Kangaroo Island and in Tasmania, canopy and rainforest walks in the Daintree, and bespoke coastal charters for whale watching and remote beaches.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Australia?
faqs.a: The best months are region-dependent: broadly, September to November and March to May offer mild weather and fewer crowds across many regions. For the northern tropics and Kimberley, the dry season from May to October is ideal, while reef visibility for snorkeling and diving is often best in the winter to spring months.

faqs.q: Is Australia safe for travelers?
faqs.a: Australia has strong tourist infrastructure and is generally safe, but conditions vary by environment: follow guidance for sun protection, ocean safety (rips and jellyfish in some areas), and remote travel logistics. Observe local biosecurity rules and respect Indigenous cultural sites and signage.

faqs.q: How many days do you need in Australia?
faqs.a: To explore one region properly, plan at least 7 to 10 days; to combine major contrasts, such as the reef and the Red Centre, allow 10 to 14 days or more. Longer itineraries of two to three weeks let you travel at a slower pace and include remote or expedition elements.

faqs.q: What is Australia famous for?
faqs.a: Australia is known for the Great Barrier Reef, vast outback landscapes, unique wildlife like kangaroos and koalas, vibrant coastal cities, and ancient Indigenous cultural sites and rock art. Its diversity ranges from tropical rainforests to temperate islands and arid deserts.

faqs.q: Land and wildlife: signature land experiences, recommended days on land, and the best regions to stay?
faqs.a: Signature land experiences include guided bushwalks and nocturnal wildlife spotting, immersive outback camps and Indigenous cultural visits, and island and forest stays for birding and endemic species viewing. For a meaningful land-based program expect 7 to 10 days per region, with 10 to 14 days recommended to combine distinct ecosystems. Top regions for wildlife and landscape variety include the Red Centre, Kangaroo Island, Tasmania, the Daintree and Cape York, Kakadu and Arnhem Land, and the Kimberley coast.

faqs.q: Cruising and diving: small-expedition ships vs large cruise lines, ocean vs river cruising, and best months for cruising?
faqs.a: Small expedition vessels and private charters are the preferred choice for remote coasts like the Kimberley and for intimate reef access, while larger cruise ships serve popular coastal and island routes with extensive onboard amenities. River cruising is limited but possible on the Murray and select waterways, offering a different, relaxed perspective. Best months for coastal cruising and tropical diving are generally April to November, when seas are calmer and water visibility is better in the tropics.

countries.name: Austria
countries.subtitle: Alpine summers, snow in winter and a country made for trains
countries.leading: Alpine valleys, lakes you can swim in, old abbeys and twelve UNESCO World Heritage properties, from the Historic Centre of Vienna to the Hallstatt-Dachstein Salzkammergut. The house starts in Styria, in the pilgrim town of Mariazell, where people have walked the Via Sacra to the basilica for 800 years.

story.eyebrow: Alpine summers, snow in winter and a country made for trains
story.title: Mountains, Lakes and Old Roads

blocks.p: Austria works in two seasons. Summer is for hiking, mountain biking and swimming in its bathing lakes; winter is for skiing, cross-country tracks, snowshoeing and tobogganing. Six international airports serve the country: Vienna, Salzburg, Innsbruck, Graz, Linz and Klagenfurt. Trains carry you most of the way, and from Vienna airport the REX7 reaches Wien Hauptbahnhof in about 20 minutes.

image.alt: Austria: Mountains, Lakes and Old Roads

story.title: Styria, Mariazell and the Heritage Cities

blocks.p: Mariazell sits in northern Styria between the Hochschwab and the Ötscher. For 800 years pilgrims have walked the Via Sacra here, past churches, monasteries and chapels, to the basilica; the Mariazell trails run through Lower Austria, Styria and Upper Austria. The house's stay here is Montestyria, a cluster of chalets above the town.

The Old Town of Graz and Schloss Eggenberg form one UNESCO World Heritage property; Eggenberg has 24 state rooms. The Dachstein, at 2,995 metres, is Styria's highest mountain. Gesäuse is Austria's youngest national park, and the library at Admont Abbey holds 70,000 restored books.

Austria has 12 properties on the UNESCO World Heritage List, among them the Historic Centre of Vienna, the Palace and Gardens of Schönbrunn, the Historic Centre of the City of Salzburg, the Hallstatt-Dachstein / Salzkammergut Cultural Landscape, the Wachau Cultural Landscape and the Semmering Railway.

image.alt: Austria: Styria, Mariazell and the Heritage Cities

facts: Best months
Summer for hiking, biking and lake swimming; winter for skiing, cross-country tracks and snowshoeing. At Montestyria the sky pool is heated from May to October.
Getting there

Six international airports: Vienna, Salzburg, Innsbruck, Graz, Linz and Klagenfurt. From Vienna airport the REX7 reaches Wien Hauptbahnhof in about 20 minutes; Mariazell is about two hours by road from Vienna or Graz.
Who it suits
Couples and families who want mountain air, lakes and quiet, in summer or in snow, with Vienna or Graz a short drive away.
Signature experiences
Walking the Via Sacra to Mariazell basilica, swimming at the Erlaufsee, Graz's Old Town and Schloss Eggenberg, the Dachstein Glacier World and the Wachau.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Austria?
faqs.a: It depends on what you want. Summer is the season for hiking, mountain biking and swimming in Austria's bathing lakes. Winter brings skiing, cross-country skiing, snowshoe hiking and tobogganing, and Advent brings the Christmas markets. Montestyria in Mariazell is open for both, with its sky pool heated from May to October.

faqs.q: How do you get to Austria?
faqs.a: Austria has six international airports: Vienna-Schwechat, the main hub, plus Salzburg, Innsbruck, Graz, Linz and Klagenfurt. From Vienna airport the REX7 regional express reaches Wien Hauptbahnhof in about 20 minutes. Montestyria says Mariazell is about two hours by road from Vienna, Graz and Linz, and can also be reached on the Mariazell train.

faqs.q: What is Mariazell known for?
faqs.a: Mariazell, in northern Styria, is Austria's great pilgrimage town. For 800 years people have walked the Via Sacra past churches, monasteries and chapels to its basilica, and a network of Mariazell trails runs through Lower Austria, Styria and Upper Austria.

faqs.q: How many UNESCO World Heritage sites does Austria have?
faqs.a: Twelve, according to UNESCO. They include the Historic Centre of Vienna, the Palace and Gardens of Schönbrunn, the Historic Centre of the City of Salzburg, the City of Graz with Schloss Eggenberg, the Hallstatt-Dachstein / Salzkammergut Cultural Landscape, the Wachau, the Semmering Railway and the Fertö / Neusiedlersee Cultural Landscape.

faqs.q: What else is there to see in Styria?
faqs.a: Graz's Old Town and Schloss Eggenberg, the Dachstein at 2,995 metres with its Glacier World reached by gondola from Ramsau, Gesäuse National Park, the 70,000-book library of Admont Abbey, Riegersburg Castle and the Lipizzaner stud at Piber.

countries.name: Bahamas
countries.subtitle: Where the Ocean Sets the Pace
countries.leading: Soft sand beaches, shallow turquoise waters, and islands scattered across warm seas define this idyllic archipelago. The landscape feels airy and bright, shaped by coral shallows and gentle tides. Stays offer barefoot tranquility and oceanfront elegance. Swim with vibrant marine life, sail between cays, or simply unwind under the glow of afternoon sun. The Bahamas invite ease, clarity, and coastal calm.

story.eyebrow: Where the Ocean Sets the Pace
story.title: A Collection of Islands, Reefs, and Endless Blue

blocks.p: The Bahamas is an archipelago of over 700 islands, where crystal clear waters, white sand beaches, and vibrant coral reefs create one of the Caribbean’s most breathtaking escapes. From secluded cays to world famous blue holes, every island offers its own blend of natural beauty and relaxed island living.

Travel here is about embracing the sea. Snorkeling colorful reefs, sailing between untouched islands, and unwinding on quiet beaches reveal a rhythm that feels effortless, peaceful, and deeply restorative.
For those seeking turquoise waters and laid back luxury, the Bahamas offers an experience that is both refreshing and unforgettable.

Journeys are designed with local expertise and access to private islands, marine parks, and authentic coastal experiences, creating stays that feel seamless, exclusive, and deeply connected to the ocean.

countries.name: Belize
countries.subtitle: The Rainforest
countries.leading: Belize rewards travelers who do more than one thing well. A few nights inland — waterfalls, forest trails and the hidden cave systems of the Maya world — then the Caribbean: private islands, overwater accommodation and the second-largest barrier reef on earth. facts: Best months
May to November for clear, dry days and the best stargazing (cold nights). December to April is the wet season, when a skin of water on the Uyuni salt flat turns it into a mirror.
Getting there
Cross overland from San Pedro de Atacama in Chile (fly into Calama, CJC), or fly into La Paz (El Alto, LPB) and on to Uyuni (UYU), about an hour by air.
Who it suits
Couples, photographers and stargazers who want the Atacama and Uyuni as one journey; walkers and travellers comfortable with high altitude.
Signature experiences
The Uyuni salt flat at dawn and under the stars; the Altiplano lagoons with their flamingos; the crossing from the Atacama; Potosí and Sucre, both UNESCO World Heritage cities.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Bolivia's salt flats?
faqs.a: May to November for dry, clear days and the best night skies, though nights are very cold. December to April is the wet season: shallow water on the Salar de Uyuni can turn it into a mirror, but some routes close after heavy rain.

faqs.q: Can you combine the Atacama Desert and the Uyuni salt flat?
faqs.a: Yes. The classic route crosses from San Pedro de Atacama in Chile over the Altiplano, past the coloured lagoons of the Eduardo Avaroa reserve, to Uyuni in Bolivia. Private crossings with lodges along the way take around a week; flying into Calama and out of Uyuni avoids doubling back.

faqs.q: Is altitude a problem in Bolivia?
faqs.a: It can be. The Altiplano and Uyuni sit around 3,600 metres and the lagoons higher still, so plan gentle first days, drink water and start low: beginning in San Pedro de Atacama (about 2,400 metres) and climbing gradually helps.

faqs.q: Is Uyuni good for stargazing?
faqs.a: Yes. High altitude, very dry air and almost no light pollution make the salt flat and the Altiplano some of the best stargazing anywhere; the dry months, away from the full moon, are best.

faqs.q: Which UNESCO World Heritage sites are near Uyuni?
faqs.a: The City of Potosí (inscribed 1987) and the Historic City of Sucre (1991) are the closest; across the border in Chile are the Humberstone and Santa Laura Saltpeter Works (2005) and the Chinchorro mummification sites near Arica (2021).

blocks.p: Brazil does not fit in one trip, and it shouldn't try. The house starts with water, the Amazon around Manaus or the Pantanal for jaguars, then adds Iguaçu, Rio or the coast at the end. story.title: The Amazon, the Pantanal, Iguaçu and Rio

blocks.h: The Amazon: Manaus and the Rio Negro
blocks.p: Manaus is the way in. Below the city the dark Rio Negro meets the pale Solimões, and for a stretch the two run side by side before they mix. Upriver, Anavilhanas National Park at Novo Airão, up to four hours by road from Manaus, holds one of the largest river archipelagos in the world. UNESCO lists it in the Central Amazon Conservation Complex, with pink river dolphins, giant otters, manatees and the arapaima. From March to August the forest floods and you go by canoe through the igapó. From September to February the water drops and the beaches come up.

One of the largest wetlands in the world, in UNESCO's words, spread across Mato Grosso and Mato Grosso do Sul. ICMBio counts 463 bird species and 124 mammals. From October to April the rivers spill over and flood the plain. When the water draws back into the rivers and small lakes, the house goes looking for jaguars. UNESCO says the Pantanal Conservation Area, on the Bolivian border, probably has the largest jaguar population in the region.

The Iguaçu River forms the border with Argentina here, in the state of Paraná. The falls run nearly three kilometres wide, with drops of up to 80 metres; the best known is the Garganta do Diabo, the Devil's Throat. Iguaçu was the first Brazilian park inscribed by UNESCO as natural World Heritage, in 1986. A day or two is enough.

blocks.h: Rio de Janeiro and the coast
blocks.p: Rio sits between the sea and Tijuca National Park, the most visited federal protected area in Brazil, with about two million visitors a year and Christ the Redeemer inside it. Walk the forest in the morning and finish on the beach. For the slow end of a trip, Trancoso and the southern Bahia coast are reached through Porto Seguro, and the Santa Catarina coast further south has quieter bays and islands.

image.alt: Brazil: The Amazon, the Pantanal, Iguaçu and Rio

facts: Best months
Amazon, high water: March to August. Amazon, low water: September to February. Pantanal, dry season: May to September.
Getting there

Fly into São Paulo Guarulhos (GRU) or Rio de Janeiro Galeão (GIG). Domestic flights connect to Manaus (MAO) for the Amazon, Cuiabá (CGB) or Campo Grande (CGR) for the Pantanal, Foz do Iguaçu (IGU) for the falls and Porto Seguro (BPS) for Trancoso.
Who it suits
Couples, families and photographers who want wildlife and water first, river dolphins and flooded forest in the Amazon or jaguars in the Pantanal, then a few days of falls, city or beach.
Signature experiences
A canoe through flooded igapó forest in Anavilhanas, the meeting of the waters below Manaus, jaguars on the Pantanal rivers, the Devil's Throat at Iguaçu and the forest trails of Tijuca above Rio.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit the Brazilian Amazon?
faqs.a: Both seasons work; they are different trips. High water runs March to August: the forest floods and you explore the igapó by canoe. Low water runs September to February: the rivers drop and the beaches come up along the Rio Negro. That is the pattern at Anavilhanas, above Manaus.

faqs.q: When is the best time to see jaguars in the Pantanal?
faqs.a: May to September, the dry season. From October to April the rains flood the plain. As the water draws back into the rivers and small lakes, wildlife has fewer places to be, and jaguars are easier to find from a boat. UNESCO notes the Pantanal Conservation Area probably holds the largest jaguar population in the region.

faqs.q: How do you get to Brazil and the Amazon?
faqs.a: Most international flights land at São Paulo Guarulhos (GRU) or Rio de Janeiro Galeão (GIG). For the Amazon, connect to Manaus (MAO); Anavilhanas is up to four hours from there by road. For the Pantanal, fly to Cuiabá (CGB) or Campo Grande (CGR).

faqs.q: Should you choose an Amazon river cruise or a lodge?
faqs.a: A cruise moves every day and covers more river: the Rio Negro, Anavilhanas and the side channels by skiff, with your cabin coming along. A lodge stays put, so you get to know one stretch of forest on foot and by canoe. The Amazon basin runs through Peru, Ecuador and Brazil, and the house has river voyages in each, set out on the Voyages side.

faqs.q: How many days do you need in Brazil?
faqs.a: Ten to fourteen days covers two or three regions: four nights in the Amazon or the Pantanal, two at Iguaçu and the rest in Rio or on the coast. Distances are long and most moves are a domestic flight, so allow three or four days per region.

faqs.q: Can you combine the Amazon with Iguaçu or Rio?
faqs.a: Yes, and most trips do. Fly from Manaus to Foz do Iguaçu (IGU) or Rio, usually with a connection. Iguaçu needs a day or two; the falls form the border with Argentina. Finish in Rio, or on the coast at Trancoso through Porto Seguro.

countries.leading: A state of sweeping contrasts: wind-sculpted coastlines, ancient redwood cathedrals, high alpine lakes, and stark desert basins. California rewards journeys that linger, connecting distinct regions through carefully paced, locally grounded experiences.

story.title: Landscape Variety and Curated Discovery

blocks.p: California condenses an extraordinary range of landscapes into a single itinerary: Pacific cliffs and surf, temperate rainforests of coastal redwoods, granite canyons and alpine ridges, and deserts whose night skies feel infinite. Each region has its own rhythm and light, which a deliberately planned journey reveals in layers rather than in snapshots.

Curated travel here is about access, timing, and local perspective: a sunrise walk beneath ancient trees, a private tasting at a small family winery, a photographer’s vantage point for a migrating whale, or a guide-led traverse of a quiet backcountry trail. Plan your route with Wild & Co. Safaris and create an experience that joins place, pace, and point of view, rather than a list of sights ticked off a map.

story.title: Regional Routes and Signature Moments

blocks.p: Drive iconic stretches of the Pacific Coast Highway and Big Sur, stopping for cliffside viewpoints, hidden coves, and seasonal whale watching along the central coast in winter and spring. Coastal stays range from intimate coastal cottages to high-end inns with curated excursions.

Experience old-growth redwood groves along the North Coast and the giant sequoias in the Sierra foothills through guided walks and quiet, early-morning access. Small-group and private walks allow for close study of forest ecology and photographic time without crowds.

From Yosemite’s granite cathedral walls and valley trails to Lake Tahoe’s alpine lakes and Sierra backcountry, there are multiday trekking, climbing, and seasonal skiing opportunities. Local guides provide route planning, permit support, and access to less-trafficked trails.

Joshua Tree and Death Valley offer stark, otherworldly landscapes and exceptional stargazing, while Napa and Sonoma provide world-class, small-production wine experiences and private cellar tours. These contrasts let you move from quiet desert nights to curated culinary moments in a single journey.

Wild & Co. Safaris travel designers assemble these elements into layered itineraries: private guides, timed park access, regional drivers, and small-group or exclusive experiences that prioritize connection to place and a measured pace of travel.

facts: Best months
April to May and September to November for mild weather and fewer crowds; summer for high-country access and coastal activities; winter for Sierra snow and southern mild climates.
Getting there

Pacific Coast drives and lighthouse viewpoints, whale watching during migration, redwood forest immersion, Yosemite climbing and valley walks, Sierra alpine lakes and winter sports, private tastings in Napa and Sonoma, desert night skies and rock-forming landscapes.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit California?
faqs.a: Spring (April to May) and fall (September to November) offer mild weather, lower crowds, and excellent light for photography; summer is ideal for high-country access and coastal escapes; winter provides snow sports in the Sierra and milder conditions in southern regions.

faqs.q: Is California safe for travelers?
faqs.a: Yes, most areas are safe with standard travel precautions for cities and remote areas. Visitors should monitor seasonal risks such as wildfires, heat in desert regions, and local advisories for air quality or park conditions.

faqs.q: How many days do you need in California?
faqs.a: A focused regional trip can be meaningful in 5 to 7 days, but 10 to 14 days allows time to combine coast, a national park, and a wine or desert region without feeling rushed.

faqs.q: What is California famous for?
faqs.a: California is known for its dramatic Pacific coastline, iconic national parks like Yosemite and Sequoia, world-class wine regions, vibrant coastal culture, and diverse outdoor recreation from surfing to alpine climbing.

faqs.q: What are the signature land experiences in California?
faqs.a: Signature experiences include driving the Pacific Coast Highway and Big Sur, walking among old-growth redwoods, hiking and photography in Yosemite and the Sierra, private wine tastings in Napa and Sonoma, and desert stargazing in Joshua Tree or Death Valley.

faqs.q: How many days should I spend on land and are there guided walking or trekking options?
faqs.a: Plan 3 to 5 days per region for meaningful exploration; guided day hikes, multi-day backcountry treks, and private guided walks are widely available, with permits required for some backcountry routes and popular park trails.

countries.name: Chile & Easter Island
countries.subtitle: Why Journey To Chile & Easter Island
countries.leading: From the driest deserts on Earth to ice-carved fjords and a singular Polynesian culture, Chile and Easter Island offer landscapes and histories that feel entirely their own. Journeys here prize remoteness, local knowledge, and slow, thoughtful travel rather than rushing through highlights.

story.eyebrow: Why Journey To Chile & Easter Island
story.title: A Country of Contrasts: Desert, Ice, Ocean, and Living Tradition

blocks.p: Chile compresses a world of extremes into a single spine of land: high, starlit altiplanos and salt flats in the north, central valleys and vineyards that cradle history and craft, and the wild southern fjords and glaciers of Patagonia. Offshore, Rapa Nui, or Easter Island, preserves a living Polynesian culture and the silent presence of moai, stone figures whose scale and placement are uniquely moving.

Travel with Wild & Co. Safaris is not about ticking boxes, it is about designing time and access. Whether that means private nights under Atacama skies with an astronomer, boat passages through the channels of the Southern Ice Field, or culturally led visits across Rapa Nui with local guardians, each itinerary prioritizes meaningful encounters over mass visitation. The result is a journey that feels remote, intentional, and unmistakably personal.

image.alt: Chile & Easter Island: A Country of Contrasts: Desert, Ice, Ocean, and Living Tradition

story.eyebrow: Find Your Edge Of The World
story.title: How Chile and Easter Island Reward Slow, Curated Travel

blocks.p: Patagonia rewards travelers who linger: guided day treks in Torres del Paine, boat rides beneath hanging glaciers, and multi-day circumnavigations of fjords reveal scale and movement that single-day visits miss. Remote estancias and small lodges place you close to the land and the people who live in it.

Easter Island is best experienced with local guidance: visits to quarry sites, stone workshops, and ceremonial platforms accompanied by Rapanui hosts illuminate the island’s living traditions and the moai in their cultural context. Private time at key sites avoids crowds and deepens understanding.

The Atacama high plateau presents landscapes that feel otherworldly by day and astronomically pristine by night. Small-group excursions to salt flats, altiplanic lagoons, and rhyolite canyons make room for slow photography, geology-led interpretation, and nocturnal observatories away from tourist hubs.

Chile’s Pacific coast and southern channels are best explored on small expedition vessels or private yachts that can navigate narrow fjords and land at shorelines inaccessible to larger ships. These voyages combine marine wildlife watching, zodiac landings, and island-hopping with expert naturalists and local pilots.

image.alt: Chile & Easter Island: How Chile and Easter Island Reward Slow, Curated Travel

facts: Best months

Patagonia: October to April for milder conditions and longer days. Atacama: clear skies year-round, with particularly stable stargazing in the cooler, dry months. Easter Island: October to March for warmer weather and cultural activity, with February hosting the Tapati Rapa Nui festival in many years.
Getting there

Santiago Arturo Merino Benitez Airport is Chile’s main international gateway. Domestic flights connect Santiago to northern airports, Punta Arenas and Puerto Natales for Patagonia, and to Mataveri Airport on Easter Island. Expedition cruises and yacht departures for southern fjords commonly embark from ports such as Puerto Montt, Castro, Punta Arenas, or Valparaiso depending on the route.
Who it suits

Travelers who want remote, carefully staged experiences: wilderness trekkers, adventure seekers, photographers, cultural explorers, honeymooners seeking seclusion, families who prefer private guides and family-friendly lodges, and solo travelers looking for guided, small-group options.
Signature experiences

Stargazing and astronomy nights in Atacama, guided explorations of high-altitude salt flats and geyser fields, multi-day treks and glacier voyages in Torres del Paine and the southern ice fields, expedition sailing through Patagonian fjords with Zodiac landings, and culturally led visits to Rapa Nui to study the moai and island traditions.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Chile & Easter Island?
faqs.a: Timing depends on the region: southern Patagonia is most accessible in the austral spring and summer, generally October through April, for longer daylight and milder weather. The Atacama high plateau offers clear skies year-round for stargazing, with especially stable dry-season nights in the cooler months. Easter Island is warmest and busiest in the southern summer, October through March, with the island’s major cultural festival usually in February.

faqs.q: Is Chile & Easter Island safe for travelers?
faqs.a: Chile and Easter Island are generally safe for travelers who exercise normal precautions: watch belongings in urban areas and follow local guidance in remote environments. Remote fieldwork or sea travel requires appropriate guides and equipment, and weather in the south can change rapidly, so travel with experienced operators.

faqs.q: How many days do you need in Chile & Easter Island?
faqs.a: A meaningful trip typically runs two weeks or more to combine two contrasting regions, for example Atacama and Patagonia, or Patagonia and Easter Island with sufficient travel time. Shorter trips can focus on a single region for deeper exploration.

faqs.q: What is Chile & Easter Island famous for?
faqs.a: Chile is known for extremes: the Atacama Desert, prolific stargazing, world-class wines, and the glaciers and fjords of Patagonia. Easter Island is famed for its moai, a unique Polynesian archaeological landscape and living island culture.

faqs.q: What are the signature land experiences and how many days should I spend on land?
faqs.a: Signature land experiences include multi-day treks and wildlife viewing in Torres del Paine, glacier boat trips and shoreline hikes in southern fjords, and archaeological and cultural tours on Rapa Nui. Plan at least 4 to 7 days per major region to allow for travel time and weather windows.

faqs.q: Which areas or reserves are best to stay for land-based exploration?
faqs.a: Top choices include the Torres del Paine massif and nearby estancias for Patagonian trekking, the Atacama altiplano and Valle de la Luna for desert landscapes and stargazing, and Rapa Nui National Park on Easter Island for moai sites and cultural access. Central valley lodges work well for food, wine, and cultural stops.

faqs.q: Should I choose a small expedition cruise or a large cruise ship for Chile’s coast and islands?
faqs.a: Small expedition vessels and yachts offer the best access to narrow fjords, Zodiac landings, and wildlife-rich coves, while large cruise ships visit principal ports but cannot reach many remote channels. For hands-on exploration and flexible landings, small expedition cruising is the preferred choice.

blocks.p: Croatia's Adriatic coast runs 1,880 km on the mainland, and its islands add 4,398 km more. The Croatian National Tourist Board counts 1,244 islands, islets, cliffs and reefs, the second largest archipelago in the Mediterranean. The coast is a warm-season destination: direct flights from New York to Dubrovnik run from May to November, and many seaside hotels open in spring and close in autumn, so the house plans the south for those months.

image.alt: Croatia: A Coast of 1,244 Islands

story.title: Dubrovnik, Split, the Islands and the Parks

blocks.p: The Old City of Dubrovnik became a Mediterranean sea power from the thirteenth century onwards. It was badly damaged by an earthquake in 1667 yet kept its Gothic, Renaissance and Baroque churches, monasteries and palaces, and UNESCO inscribed it as a World Heritage site in 1979. Lokrum island, just offshore, is part of the listed property. Mljet National Park, founded in 1960, lies about 24 sea miles away, with two saltwater lakes formed from flooded karst valleys.

In Split, the ruins of Diocletian's Palace, built between the late third and early fourth centuries AD, run through the city; it has been on the UNESCO list since 1979. Trogir, an island town whose grid of streets dates back to the Hellenistic period, followed in 1997, and the Cathedral of St James in Šibenik, built between 1431 and 1535, in 2000.

On Hvar, Stari Grad Plain has stayed practically intact since Ionian Greeks from Paros settled it in the fourth century BC, and is still farmed for grapes and olives; UNESCO listed it in 2008. Kornati National Park, founded in 1980, holds 89 islands, islets and reefs, and more than three quarters of it is sea. The Vis archipelago is one of the sailing routes the tourist board points to.

Plitvice Lakes, a national park since 1949 and on the UNESCO list since 1979, is a chain of 16 lakes held back by travertine barriers. Krka National Park, founded in 1985, has the waterfalls of Skradinski buk and Roški slap. For the table: Ston's oysters and mussels, the red wines of Dingač and Postup on Pelješac, and Buzet in Istria, the town of truffles.

facts: Best months
May to October for the coast. Direct New York to Dubrovnik flights run May to November; seaside hotels are seasonal (Villa Dubrovnik opens for 2027 on 26 March).
Getting there
Six international airports, Dubrovnik among them, with direct flights from New York to Dubrovnik from May to November, plus 15 permanent and 11 seasonal international sea ports.
Who it suits
Couples, families and sailors who want walled towns, island days by boat and a long summer on the Adriatic.
Signature experiences
Dubrovnik's Old Town walls, Diocletian's Palace in Split, sailing the Kornati and Vis islands, the Krka waterfalls, Mljet's saltwater lakes, and oysters in Ston with Pelješac wine.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Croatia?
faqs.a: For the coast, May to October. Direct flights from New York to Dubrovnik run from May to November, and many seaside hotels are seasonal: Villa Dubrovnik, for example, opens for 2027 on 26 March. We plan around each stay's own season.

faqs.q: How do you get to Croatia?
faqs.a: Croatia has six international airports, Dubrovnik among them, and the Croatian National Tourist Board lists direct flights from New York to Dubrovnik from May to November. The country also has 15 permanent and 11 seasonal ports open to international sea traffic.

faqs.q: How many islands does Croatia have?
faqs.a: The Croatian National Tourist Board counts 1,244 islands, islets, cliffs and reefs: 602 islands and islets and 642 cliffs and reefs. It is the second largest archipelago in the Mediterranean, and the islands add 4,398 km to the coastline.

faqs.q: What are Croatia's UNESCO World Heritage sites?
faqs.a: Croatia has 10 World Heritage properties. On the coast they include the Old City of Dubrovnik and Diocletian's Palace in Split (both 1979), the Historic City of Trogir (1997), the Cathedral of St James in Šibenik (2000) and Stari Grad Plain on Hvar (2008). Inland, Plitvice Lakes National Park was listed in 1979.

faqs.q: Which national parks are worth adding to a coastal trip?
faqs.a: Croatia has eight national parks. From the coast, the easiest are Krka, with the Skradinski buk waterfalls; Kornati, 89 islands, islets and reefs best seen by boat; and Mljet, about 24 sea miles from Dubrovnik, with its two saltwater lakes. Plitvice Lakes lies inland, near the road between Zagreb and Dalmatia.

faqs.q: What should you eat and drink in Croatia?
faqs.a: Oysters and mussels from Ston, the red wines of Dingač and Postup on the Pelješac peninsula, and truffles in Istria, where Buzet is known as the town of truffles. From Dubrovnik, Villa Dubrovnik's concierge arranges Pelješac wine tours.

countries.name: Dominica
countries.subtitle: Nine volcanoes, 365 rivers and a boiling lake
countries.leading: Dominica is the Caribbean's volcanic island: nine volcanoes, rainforest to the shore, rivers and waterfalls in every valley and a lake that boils. It is not a beach island. The house sends walkers, divers and people who want the Caribbean before it was tidied up.

story.eyebrow: Nine volcanoes, 365 rivers and a boiling lake
story.title: The Nature Island

blocks.p: Dominica counts nine volcanoes, 365 rivers and 29 waterfalls, and the longest hiking trail in the Caribbean runs the length of it. Morne Trois Pitons National Park, in the south central highlands, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site: nearly 7,000 hectares of tropical forest around a 1,342 metre volcano, with fumaroles, hot springs and bubbling mud.

At its heart is the Boiling Lake, the second largest in the world, a flooded fumarole that reaches 82 to 92 degrees Celsius at its edges. The walk in takes three to four hours each way through the Valley of Desolation, with a licensed guide, from Laudat, about 40 minutes from the capital, Roseau. It is a hard day and one of the great walks of the Caribbean.

image.alt: Dominica: The Nature Island

story.title: The North Coast and the South

blocks.p: Most visitors land at Douglas-Charles Airport (DOM) on the northeast coast, about an hour from the capital. Canefield (DCF), 15 minutes from Roseau, has a 3,100 foot runway for smaller aircraft.

In the north west, near Portsmouth, Secret Bay sets private villas on a clifftop above the sea. In the south west, at Soufrière, Jungle Bay is a wellness resort on a ridge of rainforest, close to the reefs at Scotts Head and Champagne Beach.

image.alt: Dominica: The North Coast and the South

facts: Getting there
Fly into Douglas-Charles Airport (DOM) on the northeast coast, where most visitors arrive, about an hour from Roseau. Canefield Airport (DCF) is 15 minutes from Roseau and takes smaller aircraft.
Who it suits
Hikers, divers and nature travellers; couples who want rainforest and a private villa more than a long white beach.
Signature experiences
The guided trek to the Boiling Lake through the Valley of Desolation, Morne Trois Pitons National Park, waterfalls and hot springs, and the reefs of the south west coast.

faqs.q: Which airport do you fly into for Dominica?
faqs.a: Douglas-Charles Airport (DOM), on the northeast side of the island about an hour from Roseau, is where most visitors arrive. Canefield Airport (DCF), 15 minutes from Roseau, has a shorter 3,100 foot runway.

faqs.q: What is the Boiling Lake?
faqs.a: A flooded volcanic fumarole in Morne Trois Pitons National Park and the second largest boiling lake in the world, reaching 82 to 92 degrees Celsius at its edges. The trek takes three to four hours each way through the Valley of Desolation and needs a licensed guide.

faqs.q: Is Dominica a UNESCO World Heritage destination?
faqs.a: Yes. Morne Trois Pitons National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site: nearly 7,000 hectares of tropical forest and volcanic features around the 1,342 metre Morne Trois Pitons.

faqs.q: Is Dominica good for beaches?
faqs.a: It is better for rainforest, rivers and reefs. Most of the island's beaches are stone or natural black sand, and the reasons to come are the walking, the hot springs and the diving.

countries.subtitle: National parks, World Heritage and the English countryside
countries.leading: England runs from the fells and lakes of the Lake District to the fossil beaches of the Jurassic Coast, with Roman Bath, Georgian country houses and old estates in between. The house's English stays sit in the Somerset countryside and in the Churnet Valley on the edge of the Peak District.

story.eyebrow: National parks, World Heritage and the English countryside
story.title: Fells, Coasts and Country Estates

blocks.p: VisitBritain describes the Lake District as a national park with England's tallest peak and its deepest lake; UNESCO inscribed it as The English Lake District in 2017. In the south west, the Dorset and East Devon Coast, the Jurassic Coast, has been a World Heritage site since 2001, its beaches and rocks strewn with fossils. Stonehenge, Avebury and Associated Sites were inscribed in 1986 and the City of Bath, with its Roman origins and Georgian streets, in 1987.

Between them lie the Peak District, Dartmoor and Exmoor, the North York Moors, the Yorkshire Dales, Northumberland, the South Downs, the New Forest and the Broads, a country of moor, chalk downland, heather and fen.

story.title: Somerset and the Peak District Edge

blocks.p: VisitBritain's Somerset is rolling hills and ancient woodland. The Newt in Somerset is a working estate built around Hadspen House, a seventeenth century house later remodelled in the Georgian style, with 30 acres of formal gardens, a spa and its own farm, cyder and restaurants.

The Tawny sits on the 70 acre Consall Estate in Staffordshire's Churnet Valley, on the edge of the Peak District, with treehouses, boathouses and shepherds' huts, each with a private outdoor spa bath. To the north east, Derbyshire holds the Derwent Valley Mills, a World Heritage site since 2001, Haddon Hall at Bakewell and the four show caves of Castleton.

faqs.q: Which UNESCO World Heritage sites are in England?
faqs.a: England's World Heritage sites include Stonehenge, Avebury and Associated Sites (1986), Durham Castle and Cathedral (1986), the City of Bath (1987), Blenheim Palace (1987), the Tower of London (1988), Canterbury Cathedral (1988), Maritime Greenwich (1997), the Derwent Valley Mills (2001), the Dorset and East Devon Coast (2001), the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew (2003), the Cornwall and West Devon Mining Landscape (2006) and The English Lake District (2017).

faqs.q: What national parks and protected landscapes does England have?
faqs.a: VisitEngland and VisitBritain name the Lake District, the Peak District, Dartmoor, Exmoor, the North York Moors, the Yorkshire Dales, Northumberland, the South Downs, the New Forest and the Broads among England's national landscapes, along with the Cotswolds and the Jurassic Coast.

faqs.q: Where are the house's stays in England?

faqs.q: What time zone and currency does England use?
faqs.a: England uses pounds sterling (GBP). Clocks are on GMT in winter and GMT+1 in summer. London is the capital.

faqs.q: Can you combine England with Scotland?
faqs.a: Yes. Scotland's international airports are Aberdeen, Edinburgh, Glasgow, Glasgow Prestwick and Inverness, and VisitScotland notes that Newcastle is just over an hour's drive from the Scottish border. James plans both countries as one journey.

countries.subtitle: Where the Ocean Feels Like Home
countries.leading: Turquoise waters, soft coral reefs, and palm lined shores create a landscape shaped by warmth and gentle rhythm. facts: Best months

Year round. The dry season, May to October, is cooler (most days 19 to 28°C) and brings the clearest water for diving, often 20 to 40 m. The wet season, November to April, is warmer (up to 31°C) with short afternoon downpours. Cloudbreak's swell season runs through the southern winter, roughly April to October; humpback whales pass through the Bligh Water from July to October; Tourism Fiji suggests June to August at Rainbow Reef for mantas and whales.
Getting there

Most international flights land at Nadi International Airport (NAN) on Viti Levu; a few use Nausori near Suva. Fiji Airways flies nonstop from Los Angeles and San Francisco (about 10h30), Dallas (about 13h, 3 a week), Honolulu (about 6h50) and Vancouver (about 11h30), and from Australia, New Zealand and Asia. Air New Zealand, Qantas, Virgin Australia and Jetstar also fly to Nadi. Islands are reached by boat from Port Denarau, by helicopter or seaplane from Nadi, or by Fiji Link and Northern Air domestic flights.
Who it suits
Honeymooners on small adults only islands, families in the Mamanucas and on Malolo, divers bound for Beqa Lagoon, the Bligh Water and Taveuni's Rainbow Reef, and surfers heading for Cloudbreak.
Signature experiences

The Beqa Lagoon shark dive in the Shark Reef Marine Reserve; Rainbow Reef and the Great White Wall in the Somosomo Strait; the Bligh Water and Namena Marine Reserve; Cloudbreak and the Mamanuca reef passes; Levuka, Fiji's UNESCO World Heritage port town on Ovalau.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Fiji?
faqs.a: Fiji works year round. May to October is the dry season, cooler and clearer for diving; November to April is warmer and wetter, with short afternoon showers.

faqs.q: Do US and Canadian travelers need a visa for Fiji?
faqs.a: US and Canadian citizens are on Fiji's visa exempt list and receive a visitor permit on arrival. You need a passport valid for at least six months beyond your stay, a return or onward ticket, and a completed arrival card. Check the Fiji Immigration visa exempt list for other passports before you book.

faqs.q: How do I fly to Fiji?
faqs.a: Most flights land at Nadi International Airport (NAN). Fiji Airways flies nonstop from Los Angeles and San Francisco in about 10 hours 30 minutes, and from Dallas, Honolulu and Vancouver.

faqs.q: How do you get between Fiji's islands?
faqs.a: Boats and catamarans leave Port Denarau daily for the Mamanuca and Yasawa islands; helicopters and seaplanes fly from Nadi; Fiji Link and Northern Air fly to the outer islands, including Savusavu on Vanua Levu.

faqs.q: How many islands does Fiji have?
faqs.a: 333, most of them ancient volcanoes. The main groups are Viti Levu, Vanua Levu, Taveuni, the Mamanuca and Yasawa islands, Lomaiviti, Lau and Kadavu.

faqs.q: Where is the best diving in Fiji?
faqs.a: Beqa Lagoon for the shark dive, the Somosomo Strait for Rainbow Reef and the Great White Wall, the Bligh Water and Namena Marine Reserve, and Kadavu's Great Astrolabe Reef.

faqs.q: Can you surf in Fiji?
faqs.a: Yes. Cloudbreak, off Tavarua and Namotu in the southern Mamanucas, is a long left reef break for experienced surfers, reached only by boat; Namotu Lefts, Swimming Pools and Wilkes Passage are nearby, and Frigates Passage lies off the Coral Coast.

faqs.q: Does Fiji have a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
faqs.a: Yes. Levuka Historical Port Town on Ovalau was inscribed in 2013 as a late colonial Pacific port town.

countries.name: Guatemala
countries.subtitle: Maya temples, a colonial city and a volcanic lake
countries.leading: Tikal in the forest, Antigua under its volcanoes, Lake Atitlán in its caldera. Guatemala is less than 500 km from north to south, but the mountain roads are slow, so the house splits it in two: the Petén by air, the highlands by road.

story.eyebrow: Maya temples, a colonial city and a volcanic lake
story.title: Two Trips, One Short Flight Apart

blocks.p: Guatemala looks small on the map. It isn't, once you're on the road. The house treats it as two trips joined by a one-hour flight: the lowland Petén, with Tikal and Lake Petén Itzá, and the highlands, with Antigua and Lake Atitlán. November to April is the dry season. May to October brings the rain, greener forest and fewer people.

image.alt: Guatemala: Two Trips, One Short Flight Apart

story.title: Tikal, Flores, Antigua and Atitlán

blocks.p: Tikal National Park covers 57,600 hectares of forest, wetland and savannah in the Petén, and UNESCO lists it for both its Maya city and its wildlife: five wild cats, howler and spider monkeys and more than 300 bird species. The city was lived in from about 600 BC until around 900 AD. Go at first light, before the heat.

Flores sits on a small island in Lake Petén Itzá, joined to Santa Elena by a bridge and a few minutes from Mundo Maya International Airport. The lake covers about 99 km² and is more than 150 metres deep in places, and you can swim in it. Tikal is about 65 km away by road. Yaxhá and Uaxactún are day trips from here too.

Antigua was the capital of the Captaincy-General of Guatemala until the Santa Marta earthquakes of 1773 moved it to what is now Guatemala City. What stayed is a grid of cobbled streets at about 1,500 metres, churches with low bell towers built for earthquakes, and the ruins of the ones that fell. UNESCO inscribed it in 1979. La Aurora airport is 45 minutes to an hour and a half away.

Lake Atitlán fills a volcanic caldera formed about 84,000 years ago, under the San Pedro, Tolimán and Atitlán volcanoes. It is 2.5 to 4 hours by road from Guatemala City. Panajachel is the way in, and boats run from its docks to San Marcos La Laguna, San Juan La Laguna, Santiago Atitlán and the other Maya towns on the shore.

image.alt: Guatemala: Tikal, Flores, Antigua and Atitlán

facts: Best months
Dry season November to April, the most popular months for Tikal, Antigua and Lake Atitlán. The rains start in May and last into October: greener forest, afternoon showers and fewer visitors.
Getting there

Fly into La Aurora International Airport (GUA) in Guatemala City, 45 minutes to an hour and a half from Antigua. Daily flights of about an hour connect Guatemala City with Mundo Maya International Airport (FRS) at Flores, for Tikal. By road from Belize, the crossing is Melchor de Mencos.
Who it suits
Couples, families, photographers and walkers who want Maya history and living Maya towns in one trip, with time on the water between the ruins.
Signature experiences
Tikal at first light, a swim in Lake Petén Itzá, Holy Week processions over sawdust carpets in Antigua, and a boat between the Maya towns of Lake Atitlán.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Guatemala?
faqs.a: November to April, the dry season, when Tikal's trails are in better shape and the volcanoes around Lake Atitlán are clearest. May to October is the rainy season: greener and quieter, with most of the rain in the afternoon. Holy Week draws the biggest crowds, so book early.

faqs.q: How do you get to Guatemala?
faqs.a: Most international flights land at La Aurora International Airport (GUA) in Guatemala City, about 2.5 to 3 hours from Miami or Houston, with a direct flight from Madrid. For Tikal, connect to Mundo Maya International Airport (FRS) at Flores, about an hour's flight.

faqs.q: How do you get to Tikal?
faqs.a: Fly to Flores, then drive about 65 km, an hour to an hour and a half, to Tikal National Park. UNESCO listed it in 1979 for both its Maya city and its forest. Give it a full day from first light, and a night or two on Lake Petén Itzá to add Yaxhá.

faqs.q: How far is Antigua from the airport?
faqs.a: 45 minutes to an hour and a half by road from La Aurora in Guatemala City, depending on traffic. Antigua has no airport of its own. Most trips start here: the old capital sits at about 1,500 metres, is easy to walk and is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

faqs.q: How do you get to Lake Atitlán?
faqs.a: By road from Guatemala City, 2.5 to 4 hours depending on traffic and which town you stay in. Panajachel is the main gateway, and public and private boats cross from its docks to the other lakeside towns. It follows Antigua well.

faqs.q: How many days do you need in Guatemala, and can you add Belize or Mexico?
faqs.a: Allow 7 to 10 days for both halves: three or four nights in the Petén, the rest between Antigua and Lake Atitlán. Belize is next door: Flores to Belize City is 3 to 4 hours by road through the Melchor de Mencos border. From Mexico the land crossings are La Mesilla and Tecún Umán, and San Cristóbal de las Casas is 5 to 6 hours away.

story.eyebrow: Where Fire and Ice Shape the Land
story.title: A Landscape of Volcanoes, Glaciers, and Raw Elements

blocks.p: Iceland is a country still being made. Volcanoes, glaciers, black sand beaches and waterfalls sit within a few hours' drive of each other, and the land changes with every eruption and every thaw.

Travel here is about the elements: walking across lava fields, standing beside waterfalls, soaking in geothermal water under an open sky, and watching the light, which lasts almost all night in summer and gives way to the northern lights in winter.

Iceland for nature and elemental explorers Thingvellir, Surtsey and Vatnajökull National Park are on the UNESCO World Heritage List, and most of the country is reached by self-drive. We plan around the season, the roads that are open, and the stays that put you closest to the landscape.

facts: Best months

June to August is the main season. Northern lights are strongest around the March and September equinoxes. Puffins from early May to mid August; highland F-roads open mid or late June to mid September.
Getting there
Fly into Keflavík International Airport, 48 km from Reykjavík (40 to 50 minutes by Flybus), or seasonally into Akureyri in the north. Most stays are reached by self-drive.
Who it suits
Couples and active travellers who will self-drive between volcanoes, glaciers and hot water, in summer light or under winter skies.
Signature experiences
Thingvellir, a UNESCO site since 2004; Vatnajökull National Park; the northern lights at the equinoxes; puffins in summer; and a hot tub under open sky at a glass lodge.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Iceland?
faqs.a: June to August is the most popular season. Spring and autumn are short and change from year to year, and September and October are among the busiest months. The highland F-roads are usually open from mid or late June to mid September, and puffins are present from the beginning of May to the middle of August.

faqs.q: When can you see the northern lights in Iceland?
faqs.a: The equinoxes in March and September are ideal, as the lights tend to be more prominent then. They become harder to spot in April, and by the end of August the chances of seeing them are already high.

faqs.q: How do you get to Iceland?
faqs.a: Keflavík International Airport is 48 km (30 miles) from Reykjavík; the Flybus takes 40 to 50 minutes and is timed to flights, and taxis and car rental are at arrivals. Akureyri International Airport in the north has seasonal international flights, including from London and Manchester.

faqs.q: What are Iceland's UNESCO World Heritage sites?
faqs.a: Thingvellir (inscribed 2004), Surtsey (2008) and Vatnajökull National Park (2019). Vatnajökull covers over 1,400,000 hectares, nearly 14% of Iceland's territory.

faqs.q: Where are the house's stays in Iceland?

countries.subtitle: Why Journey To Ireland
countries.leading: Ireland is a country of Atlantic edges, layered history, and deeply rooted hospitality, where rugged landscapes meet lively towns and quiet country roads. story.title: A More Intimate Way to Experience the Emerald Isle

blocks.p: Ireland rewards travelers who leave room for detours. Rather than moving from landmark to landmark, a thoughtfully designed journey might trace the wild edge of Connemara, follow harbors and headlands, or travel north and west through landscapes shaped by the Atlantic. The distinction is in the pace and the detail, with time for cliffside walks, historic houses, village pubs, and the changing light that gives each region its own atmosphere.

The country’s stays make the journey feel personal. From coastal bases such as Breac.House and King Sitric to heritage properties including Castle Leslie, The Merrion, and Hayfield Manor, accommodation becomes part of the story rather than simply a place to sleep. My Epic Africa creates journeys around these contrasts, balancing Ireland’s untamed coastline with its gardens, cities, country estates, and warm local welcome.

story.title: Coastlines, Culture, and Country House Hospitality

blocks.p: Ireland’s western seaboard is defined by weather, sea, and scale. Connemara, Achill Island, the harbors and headlands of the coast, and the landscapes of North by Northwest Ireland offer a sense of space and exposure that is best experienced slowly, with scenic drives and walks shaped by the conditions of the day.

Ancient ruins, stone walls, historic estates, and old market towns make Ireland’s past part of the present journey. Places such as Castle Leslie and The Merrion add a refined sense of heritage, while regional stays in Limerick, Cahersiveen, and beyond create a closer connection to local character.

Ireland’s hospitality is often found in small, memorable moments: a conversation over dinner, traditional music in a village gathering place, or the easy warmth of a well-run guesthouse. Properties including Aiteall Boutique Accommodation, Ariel House, Number 31, and The Wilder bring distinct interpretations of that welcome.

blocks.h: A Journey With Room To Breathe
blocks.p: Ireland is particularly rewarding when an itinerary is not overfilled. A carefully crafted route can connect Dublin, the southern counties, Connemara, the Atlantic coast, and the northwest while preserving time for weather-led walks, unplanned discoveries, and evenings in characterful hotels and country retreats.

facts: Best months

May through September is generally the most favorable period for sightseeing and coastal walks. Spring and autumn can offer quieter roads and fewer visitors, but Ireland’s weather is changeable throughout the year.
Getting there

Most international visitors arrive by air into Dublin, with additional access through airports including Cork and Shannon depending on the itinerary. Ireland can also be reached by ferry from Great Britain and France, and onward travel is typically by private vehicle, rental car, or a carefully planned driver-led route.
Who it suits

Ireland suits travelers who value landscape, history, local culture, and unhurried exploration. It works particularly well for couples, families, solo travelers, and guests seeking a high-touch journey built around characterful stays rather than a standard packaged tour.
Signature experiences

Signature experiences include tracing the Atlantic coast, exploring Connemara and Achill Island, following harbors and headlands, visiting historic estates and ruins, discovering Ireland’s literary and musical traditions, and staying in distinctive properties such as Breac.House, Castle Leslie, The Merrion, Hayfield Manor, and The Wilder.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Ireland?
faqs.a: Ireland can be visited year-round. May through September generally offers the best conditions for sightseeing and coastal walks, while spring and autumn bring fewer visitors and distinctive light, though weather remains changeable in every season.

faqs.q: Is Ireland safe for travelers?
faqs.a: Ireland is generally considered a safe destination for travelers. As with any country, visitors should take normal precautions in cities, on the road, and when walking in remote coastal or rural areas.

faqs.q: How many days do you need in Ireland?
faqs.a: A week allows time to explore one or two regions without rushing. Ten to fourteen days is more suitable for combining Dublin with the south, Connemara, the Atlantic coast, or the north and northwest.

faqs.q: What is Ireland famous for?
faqs.a: Ireland is famous for its dramatic Atlantic coastline, green countryside, rich literary and musical traditions, historic ruins, castles, and welcoming hospitality. It is also known for distinctive regional landscapes, from Connemara to the western peninsulas and island communities.

faqs.q: What are the best places to visit in Ireland?
faqs.a: The best places depend on the style of journey, but compelling regions include Dublin, County Cork and Kerry, Connemara, Achill Island, Limerick, and the north and northwest. The itineraries Connemara at the Wild Edge, Harbors, Headlands & Irish Hearths, and North by Northwest Ireland are designed around these varied landscapes and local character.

faqs.q: What are the best things to do on an Ireland trip?
faqs.a: Travelers can explore coastal paths, historic estates, villages, gardens, ruins, and lively towns, while making time for traditional music and regional food. Ireland is especially well suited to scenic road journeys that combine outdoor discovery with distinctive guesthouses, hotels, and country stays.

story.title: Not the Queues, the Valleys

blocks.p: Italy is easy to do badly: five cities in eight days, a train every morning, the same piazzas as everyone else. We plan it the other way, with fewer places and longer in each.

A city at the start or the end, then three nights or more somewhere the landscape does the work: a mountain meadow, a lake, a hill farm. Every stay we send you to is filed in the Ledger, and the list grows as we vet it.
