story.title: The Dolomites, in Both Seasons

blocks.p: The Dolomites are UNESCO-listed mountains in Italy's far north. We start in South Tyrol, where the place names come in German and Italian and the food is a little of both.
From December to March the ski runs link valley to valley. From June to October the high meadows are for walking. Between the two, many mountain hotels close, so we plan around the seasons.
Bolzano has the nearest airport; Innsbruck, Venice and Munich are the larger gateways, a few hours by road.

image.alt: Italy: The Dolomites, in Both Seasons

facts: Best months

By region and season: the Dolomites December to March for skiing and June to October for walking (COMO Alpina Dolomites); island and mountain stays open seasonally (Pension Briol May to October). We plan around each stay's own season.
Getting there
Fly into Rome Fiumicino (FCO), Milan, Florence (FLR), Naples (NAP) or Venice, depending on the region; Bolzano (BZO) for the Dolomites. Most country stays are reached by car.
Who it suits
Couples and families who want food, wine, history and landscape, two or three regions at a time, and travellers tracing Italian family roots.
Signature experiences
A castle estate in the Maremma, the Val d'Orcia, the cliffs of the Amalfi Coast, a boat around Salina, and walking the high meadows of the Dolomites.

faqs.q: Where should I stay in Italy?
faqs.a: It depends on the region. In the Ledger: Castello di Vicarello, Reschio and Monteverdi for castles and hill villages in Tuscany and Umbria; Palazzo Avino and Hotel Santa Caterina on the Amalfi Coast; Capofaro on Salina in the Aeolian Islands; and COMO Alpina Dolomites, Forestis and Pension Briol in the mountains of South Tyrol.

faqs.q: How many places should I see in one Italy trip?
faqs.a: Two or three, with at least three nights in each. A city at one end, then the countryside, the coast or the mountains. Italy rewards staying put more than it rewards moving on.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit the Dolomites?
faqs.a: December to March for skiing and June to October for walking, as COMO Alpina Dolomites publishes for the Alpe di Siusi. Many mountain hotels close in between; Pension Briol, for example, opens only from May to October.

faqs.q: How many UNESCO World Heritage sites does Italy have?
faqs.a: Sixty-two, according to UNESCO, more than any other country. They include the Historic Centre of Naples (1995), the Costiera Amalfitana (1997), the Sassi of Matera (1993), Val d'Orcia (2004), the Aeolian Islands (2000) and the Dolomites (2009).

faqs.q: Can James Wild & Co plan an Italian heritage trip?
faqs.a: Yes. James's own family story begins in Naples. Start with what you know of your family's town and records; we build the route around the research and choose stays in the regions it leads to. Read his journal piece, Tracing My Italian Roots Through Five Remarkable Stays.

facts: Best months
Midnight sun above the Arctic Circle from late May to mid July (Bodø 4 June to 8 July, Lofoten 28 May to 14 July). Northern lights from September to late March in Northern Norway.
Getting there

Fly into Oslo, Bergen, Tromsø or another international airport; London to Oslo or Bergen is about 2 hours. For the northern islands, connect to Bodø and take the express boat; for the fjords, fly to Ålesund or Bergen and drive.
Who it suits

The Geirangerfjord and Nærøyfjord, a UNESCO site since 2005; the midnight sun and northern lights above the Arctic Circle; sea eagles in Steigen; and nights in architect designed cabins and treehouses.

faqs.q: When can you see the midnight sun in Norway?
faqs.a: North of the Arctic Circle the sun stays above the horizon through the height of summer. At the Arctic Circle itself it lasts from 12 June to 1 July; in Bodø from 4 June to 8 July; in Lofoten from 28 May to 14 July; in Tromsø from 20 May to 22 July; and at the North Cape from 14 May to 29 July. In the south it never gets fully dark at midsummer.

faqs.q: When is the best time to see the northern lights in Norway?
faqs.a: From September to late March, north of the Arctic Circle in Northern Norway. The lights are visible to the naked eye only when it is fully dark, and because coastal weather changes quickly, a clear sky is often a short drive away.

faqs.q: How do you get to Norway?
faqs.a: Oslo Airport is the main hub, with scheduled flights to more than 100 international destinations; Bergen, Stavanger, Tromsø, Trondheim, Kristiansand and Sandefjord also have international flights. London to Oslo or Bergen is about 2 hours and New York to Oslo about 7.5 hours. Trains run from Gothenburg and Malmö, and ferries from Denmark, Sweden and Germany.

faqs.q: What are the West Norwegian Fjords?
faqs.a: The Geirangerfjord and the Nærøyfjord, about 120 km apart northeast of Bergen, were inscribed together as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2005. Their crystalline walls rise up to 1,400 m from the water and reach 500 m below sea level, lined with waterfalls.

faqs.q: Where are the house's stays in Norway?
faqs.a: Juvet Landscape Hotel near Valldal, on the scenic route between the Geirangerfjord and Trollstigen; Manshausen and The Arctic Hideaway on islands reached by express boat from Bodø, above the Arctic Circle; and Woodnest's treehouses above Odda, about 3 hours' drive from Bergen Airport.

facts: Best months

Palawan: December to April in El Nido (calmest seas), late November to May in Coron, November to May in Puerto Princesa. Siargao: March to September for the dry season, with the biggest surf from September to November. Visayas: November to May at Apo Island, December to May at Moalboal, both per the Department of Tourism.
Getting there

Fly into Manila, Clark or Cebu, then connect. Puerto Princesa International Airport (PPS) is about 1 hour 15 minutes from Manila. AirSwift flies to Lio Airport (ENI) in El Nido, about 1 hour 20 minutes from Manila. Coron is reached by flying to Busuanga, about 1 to 1.5 hours from Manila. Sayak Airport (IAO) on Siargao is about 2 hours from Manila and 1 hour from Cebu. Dumaguete Sibulan Airport (DGT) serves Dauin and Apo Island.
Who it suits

Island seekers, surfers, divers and families who want limestone lagoons, private islands and warm Filipino hospitality, from Palawan's Bacuit Bay and Calamian Islands to Siargao's breaks and the reefs of the Visayas.
Signature experiences

Island hopping in El Nido's Bacuit Archipelago of 45 islands and islets; Coron's lagoons and 1944 wrecks; the 8.2 km Puerto Princesa Underground River, a UNESCO site; surfing Cloud 9 on Siargao; Apo Island's community marine sanctuary; the sardine run at Moalboal; Tubbataha Reefs, a UNESCO marine park in the Sulu Sea.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit the Philippines?
faqs.a: November to May is the dry season for most island areas. In El Nido the best window is December to April; in Coron, late November to May. Siargao's dry season runs March to September, and its biggest surf arrives September to November. June to October brings rain and boat cancellations.

faqs.q: Do I need a visa for the Philippines?
faqs.a: Citizens of 157 countries, including the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia and all EU states, may enter visa free for up to 30 days. You need a passport valid at least six months beyond your stay and a return or onward ticket. Extensions are made at a Bureau of Immigration office.

faqs.q: What is eTravel?
faqs.a: eTravel is the free online arrival registration every arriving traveller completes, up to 72 hours before arrival, at etravel.gov.ph, the only official site. You show the QR code before boarding and on arrival.

faqs.q: How do you get to Palawan?
faqs.a: Fly from Manila to Puerto Princesa (about 1 hour 15 minutes), to Lio Airport in El Nido on AirSwift (about 1 hour 20 minutes), or to Busuanga for Coron. Many island resorts then continue by boat.

faqs.q: What is the Puerto Princesa Underground River?
faqs.a: It is an 8.2 km navigable river through limestone caves that flows straight into the sea, inside a UNESCO World Heritage park about 76 km northwest of Puerto Princesa. Visitor numbers are capped daily, so book two to four weeks ahead, especially December to May.

faqs.q: What are the Philippines' natural UNESCO World Heritage Sites?
faqs.a: Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park, inscribed in 1993 and extended in 2006, and Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park, inscribed in 1999. The country has six World Heritage properties in all, including the Baroque Churches of the Philippines and the Rice Terraces of the Philippine Cordilleras.

countries.name: Sri Lanka
countries.subtitle: Ancient cities, tea country, leopards and two monsoons
countries.leading: Rock fortresses and cave temples in the dry zone, tea estates in the hills, a Dutch-walled fort on the south coast and leopards in the scrub at Yala. Two monsoons reach opposite coasts at different times of year, so the house plans Sri Lanka around the month.

story.eyebrow: Ancient cities, tea country, leopards and two monsoons
story.title: One Island, Two Monsoons

blocks.p: Sri Lanka's weather arrives from two directions. From December to March the northeast monsoon leaves the west and south coasts dry, with calm seas. From May to September the southwest monsoon rains on that side and on the hills, and the east coast takes its turn. March and April, between the two, suit the Cultural Triangle and the hill country. October and November bring showers anywhere. Pick the month first; the coast follows.

image.alt: Sri Lanka: One Island, Two Monsoons

story.title: Sigiriya, Kandy, Galle and Yala

blocks.p: Four UNESCO World Heritage sites sit close together in the dry zone. Sigiriya is a rock about 180 metres high that King Kassapa I made into a fortified palace in the late fifth century, with water gardens at its foot and painted women in a shelter on its western face. Climb it early, before the heat. Dambulla's five cave shrines have drawn pilgrims for some 22 centuries and hold 157 statues. Anuradhapura was the capital from the fourth century BC to the turn of the eleventh, and Polonnaruwa took over after Anuradhapura fell in 993.

Kandy was the seat of Sri Lanka's last kingdom. Its Temple of the Tooth, the Dalada Maligawa, keeps the relic Buddhists revere as the Buddha's tooth, and is one of the most sacred Buddhist sites in the country. Beyond it the central highlands are planted with tea, the air cools and the old estate bungalows still stand. The railway runs through the hill country between Kandy, Ella and Badulla; the views are the reason to take it.

Galle Fort sits on a rocky point at the island's southwest corner, 113 km from Colombo by expressway. The Portuguese founded it in the sixteenth century and the Dutch walled it; most of the ramparts date to 1663. UNESCO calls it the best representation of a fortified city built by Europeans in South Asia. East along the coast are Unawatuna, Mirissa and Tangalle. From Mirissa, boats head out towards Dondra Point for blue whales and dolphins in this coast's season, from December.

Yala, in the southeast, has one of the highest leopard densities in the world; with Wilpattu it became one of Sri Lanka's first two national parks, in 1938. Udawalawe is the place for elephants: about 500 live in the park, often in herds of up to 100, all year round. Wilpattu, in the northwest near Anuradhapura, adds leopards, sloth bears and nearly sixty natural lakes, the willus. Every park is entered on a Department of Wildlife Conservation permit. On the east coast, Trincomalee is the other whale port, in season from May to September.

facts: Best months

West and south coasts: December to March, the dry side of the northeast monsoon, with calm seas. Hill country and the Cultural Triangle: March to April, between the monsoons. East coast and Trincomalee: May to September, while the southwest monsoon rains on the other side.
Getting there

Fly into Bandaranaike International Airport (CMB) at Katunayake, the main international airport, 30 km north of Colombo. By road from Colombo, Sigiriya is about 169 km, Galle 113 km by expressway and Yala about 300 km. Mattala Rajapaksa International Airport, near Hambantota in the deep south, is the second international airport.
Who it suits
Couples, families and photographers who want ancient cities, a hill-country train, a leopard drive and a beach in one trip, and travellers adding a week before or after the Maldives.
Signature experiences

Sigiriya at first light, the Temple of the Tooth in Kandy, the hill-country railway to Ella, a leopard drive in Yala, the elephant herds of Udawalawe, Galle Fort's ramparts at sunset and blue whales off Mirissa.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Sri Lanka?
faqs.a: It depends on the coast. December to March is the season for the west and south coasts, Galle and Mirissa, with clear skies and calm seas. May to September is the east coast's turn: Trincomalee and Arugam Bay are dry while the southwest monsoon rains on the other side. March and April, between the monsoons, suit the Cultural Triangle and the hill country. October and November bring showers across the island.

faqs.q: How do you get to Sri Lanka?
faqs.a: Fly into Bandaranaike International Airport (CMB) at Katunayake, about 30 km north of Colombo; it is the main international airport. From Colombo, Sigiriya is about 169 km by road, Galle 113 km by expressway and Yala about 300 km. Mattala Rajapaksa International Airport, near Hambantota in the south, is the second international airport.

faqs.q: How many days do you need in Sri Lanka?
faqs.a: Allow 10 to 14 days for the Cultural Triangle, Kandy and the tea country, a national park and the south coast without rushing. With a week, pick two: the ancient cities and Kandy, or the hill country and the south coast with a night or two near Yala or Udawalawe. Choose the coast by the month you travel.

faqs.q: What is Sigiriya, and how do you visit it?
faqs.a: Sigiriya is a rock about 180 metres high in the Cultural Triangle, where King Kassapa I (477 to 495) built a fortified palace on the summit, with water gardens below and frescoes on the western face. UNESCO inscribed it as a World Heritage site in 1982. It is about 169 km from Colombo and 25 km from Dambulla. Start the climb as early as you can and carry water and a hat: drinks are not sold inside.

faqs.q: Where is the best place to see leopards in Sri Lanka?
faqs.a: Yala National Park, in the southeast, has one of the highest leopard densities in the world. It covers 979 km², about 300 km from Colombo, and also protects elephants and 215 bird species. Wilpattu, in the northwest near Anuradhapura, is the other leopard park. Both are entered on a Department of Wildlife Conservation permit. For elephants, Udawalawe, inland from the south coast, has about 500 in the park all year.

faqs.q: Can you combine Sri Lanka with the Maldives?
faqs.a: Yes. Sri Lanka's west and south coasts are at their best from December to March, inside the Maldives season in the Ledger (November to April). Fly into Colombo (CMB), spend a week or more on the island, then fly on to Malé for the beach. James plans both as one trip and books the Maldives stays from the Ledger.

countries.subtitle: Two peaks, a volcano you can drive into and a calm Caribbean coast
countries.leading: Saint Lucia is a volcanic island in the Eastern Caribbean, northwest of Barbados and south of Martinique, with two forest-clad spires, the Pitons, rising from the sea beside Soufrière. The house keeps to that southwest corner: rainforest, mineral springs, quiet beaches and three stays that look straight at the peaks.

story.eyebrow: Two peaks, a volcano you can drive into and a calm Caribbean coast
story.title: The Pitons and the Southwest

blocks.p: Gros Piton and Petit Piton stand beside the sea near Soufrière, on the island's southwest coast. The Pitons Management Area became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2004, for its natural beauty and its volcanic geology, and the listing covers the forests and the sea around the peaks as well as the peaks themselves.

Gros Piton is the one you climb: 798 metres, a 4 km round trip with a guide, usually four to six hours. Petit Piton is steeper and is best admired from a beach, a viewpoint or a boat. Below them lie Sulphur Springs, which the island calls the world's only drive-in volcano, the Diamond Falls Botanical Gardens, and the beaches of Anse Chastanet, Anse Mamin and Sugar Beach, white sand set between the two peaks.

image.alt: St Lucia: The Pitons and the Southwest

story.title: Soufrière, by Road or Helicopter

blocks.p: Most international flights land at Hewanorra International Airport at Vieux Fort, in the south. George F. L. Charles Airport, beside the capital Castries in the northwest, takes regional flights from neighbouring islands.

The island is warm all year, between about 23 and 31 degrees Celsius, cooled by the trade winds. December to April is the driest and busiest season; the tourism authority gives December to May for the clearest views and calmest seas on the west coast.
James and his wife honeymooned at Ladera, between the Pitons, in May 2022. It is their favourite Caribbean getaway.

faqs.q: Why are the Pitons a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
faqs.a: The Pitons Management Area was inscribed in 2004 for its exceptional natural beauty and its volcanic geology. The listing protects the wider landscape, including forests and marine areas, as well as the two peaks.

faqs.q: Can you climb the Pitons?
faqs.a: Gros Piton, yes, with a guide: it is 798 metres high, the trail is a 4 km round trip and the climb usually takes four to six hours. Petit Piton is steeper and is not generally open to casual hikers.

facts: Best months

Dry season May to October, wet season November to April, 20 to 30°C year round. Society Islands: lagoons best May to October. Tuamotu: diving all year, warmest water November to April. Marquesas: year round. Austral: whales July to October. Gambier: lagoon outings November to May. Surf at Teahupo'o: May to October southern swells (Tahiti Tourisme).
Getting there

All international flights land at Tahiti Faa'a International Airport (PPT). Nonstop from Los Angeles (about 8 hours), San Francisco (about 8h30) and Honolulu (about 6 hours). Air Tahiti then flies to all five archipelagos: Moorea in 15 minutes, Raiatea and Huahine 40 to 45, Bora Bora 50, Rangiroa 1 hour, Fakarava 1h10. Ferries cross to Moorea in about 30 minutes.
Who it suits
Couples on lagoon islands, divers in the Tuamotu passes, surfers at Teahupo'o, and travelers who want culture and hiking in the Marquesas.
Signature experiences

Diving Fakarava's Tumakohua Pass and Rangiroa's Tiputa Pass, watching Teahupo'o break, Taputapuātea on Raiatea and the Marquesas (both UNESCO World Heritage), and island hopping by air, ferry or small ship.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit French Polynesia?
faqs.a: May to October is the dry season, with sunny days and lower humidity; November to April is warmer and wetter. Diving in the Tuamotu is good all year, and Teahupo'o's big swells come May to October.

faqs.q: Do US and EU travelers need a visa for Tahiti?
faqs.a: EU citizens need no visa, and Tahiti Tourisme says many countries are exempt for tourist stays under three months. Everyone needs a valid passport. Check France's official visa site for your nationality before you book.

faqs.q: How do you fly to Tahiti?
faqs.a: Every international flight lands at Tahiti Faa'a (PPT). Nonstops run from Los Angeles in about 8 hours, San Francisco in about 8h30 and Honolulu in about 6.

faqs.q: How do you get between the islands?
faqs.a: Air Tahiti flies to all five archipelagos and sells multi island passes; ferries link Tahiti and Moorea in about 30 minutes and run to Huahine, Raiatea, Taha'a and Bora Bora two or three times a week; small ships such as Windstar and Aranui 5 cover longer routes.

faqs.q: What are the five archipelagos?
faqs.a: The Society Islands (Tahiti, Moorea, Bora Bora, Taha'a), the Tuamotu (the largest chain of atolls in the world, with Rangiroa, Fakarava and Tikehau), the Marquesas, the Austral Islands and the Gambier.

faqs.q: Is any of French Polynesia a UNESCO site?
faqs.a: Yes. Taputapuātea on Raiatea was inscribed in 2017 and Te Henua Enata, the Marquesas Islands, in 2024. Fakarava and six neighbouring atolls form a UNESCO biosphere reserve.

faqs.q: How do you get to Taha'a?
faqs.a: Taha'a has no airport. Fly from Tahiti to Raiatea with Air Tahiti, then cross the shared lagoon by boat; Tahiti Tourisme puts the crossing at about 30 minutes.

faqs.q: Can you fly from Bora Bora straight to the atolls?
faqs.a: Yes. Air Tahiti flies Bora Bora direct to Rangiroa, Tikehau and Fakarava, so a trip can go from the Society Islands to the Tuamotu without returning to Tahiti.

facts: Best months

Andaman coast (Phuket, Krabi, Phi Phi): November to April. Gulf islands (Samui, Phangan): December to June. The north (Chiang Mai, Chiang Rai): November to February, the cool season (Tourism Authority of Thailand).
Getting there

Bangkok has two international airports, Suvarnabhumi (BKK) and Don Mueang (DMK); Chiang Mai, Chiang Rai, Phuket, Hat Yai, Udon Thani and Krabi also have international airports (Tourism Authority of Thailand). From 15 September 2026, nationals of 60 countries and territories, including the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia and every EU member state, may stay up to 30 days visa free for tourism; everyone else applies at thaievisa.go.th (Tourism Authority of Thailand; Ministry of Foreign Affairs). Every non Thai national submits the Thailand Digital Arrival Card online within 3 days before arrival, with no fee (Immigration Bureau, tdac.immigration.go.th).
Who it suits
Beach and island travellers, families, wellness seekers, divers, and anyone drawn to temples, food and the hill country of the north.
Signature experiences

Phang Nga Bay's limestone karsts; the Andaman marine parks, where the Similan Islands reopened on 15 October 2026 and Maya Bay on 1 October, with e tickets at six parks (Tourism Authority of Thailand); Samui's wellness retreats; the Golden Triangle on the Mekong; and nine UNESCO World Heritage properties, from Sukhothai and Ayutthaya to the Khao Yai forests (UNESCO).

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Thailand?
faqs.a: November to February is the cool season, which the Tourism Authority of Thailand calls a fantastic time to travel. For beaches, the Andaman coast is best from November to April and the Gulf islands from December to June. Source: Tourism Authority of Thailand (tatnews.org, November 2020).

faqs.q: Which coast should I choose, Andaman or Gulf?
faqs.a: It depends on the month. Phuket, Krabi and Phi Phi on the Andaman side are best from November to April, while Samui and Phangan in the Gulf are best from December to June, so the two coasts cover most of the year between them. Source: Tourism Authority of Thailand.

faqs.q: Do I need a visa for Thailand?
faqs.a: Not for short holidays from most Western countries. Since 15 September 2026, nationals of 60 countries and territories, including the US, UK, Canada, Australia and the EU, can stay up to 30 days visa free for tourism, and land border entries under the exemption are generally limited to twice a calendar year. Others apply on the official e Visa site, thaievisa.go.th. Sources: Tourism Authority of Thailand (tatnews.org, September 2026); Ministry of Foreign Affairs (mfa.go.th, 3 September 2026).

faqs.q: What is the Thailand Digital Arrival Card?
faqs.a: An online form that replaced the paper arrival card. All non Thai nationals must submit it within 3 days before arriving, at tdac.immigration.go.th, and the official site says no fee is required. Source: Thai Immigration Bureau (tdac.immigration.go.th).

countries.subtitle: Bodrum's bays and Cappadocia's valleys
countries.leading: The Aegean bays of the Bodrum peninsula, where wooden gulets are still built, and the fairy chimneys of Cappadocia, where balloons rise at sunrise over churches cut into the rock. Türkiye has 22 properties on the UNESCO World Heritage List; the house plans around two of its most different landscapes.

story.title: Aegean Coast and Anatolian Stone

blocks.p: The house works in two parts of Türkiye. On the Aegean, the Bodrum peninsula has a harbour that has taken ships for some 3,000 years, a castle built by the Knights Hospitaller and the site of the Mausoleum of Halicarnassus. Inland, Cappadocia spreads across Nevşehir and its neighbours, a volcanic landscape of valleys, rock churches and underground cities. Fly into Milas-Bodrum for the coast; Cappadocia is a separate leg.

image.alt: Turkey: Aegean Coast and Anatolian Stone

story.title: Bodrum, Uçhisar and the Rock Sites

blocks.p: The Knights Hospitaller built Bodrum Castle, the Castle of St. Peter, in the 15th century. Since 1964 it has housed the Bodrum Museum of Underwater Archaeology, which won a special commendation as European Museum of the Year in 1995. Nearby is the site of the Mausoleum of Halicarnassus, built for the Carian satrap Mausolus, who died in 353 BCE; it stood 45 metres tall. Three-masted gulets are still built here. The house's stays are on the peninsula's north coast at Göltürkbükü, and further north at Kaplankaya.

UNESCO lists Göreme National Park and the Rock Sites of Cappadocia as a World Heritage property, a landscape of fairy chimneys, rock-hewn churches, troglodyte villages and the underground cities of Kaymaklı and Derinkuyu, bounded by Erciyes Dağ (3,916 m) and Hasan Dağ (3,253 m). The Göreme Open Air Museum's Dark Church dates from the late 11th and early 12th centuries. Uçhisar Castle is the highest viewpoint, with Pigeon Valley walking below it; Derinkuyu goes down about 85 metres.

Couples and families who want Aegean bays and Anatolian history in one trip.
Signature experiences
A sunrise balloon over Cappadocia, the Göreme Open Air Museum, Derinkuyu underground city, Bodrum Castle and its Museum of Underwater Archaeology, and a day on the water from the Bodrum peninsula.

faqs.q: What is Cappadocia known for?
faqs.a: Fairy chimneys, rock-cut churches and underground cities. UNESCO describes Göreme National Park and the Rock Sites of Cappadocia as one of the world's largest cave-dwelling complexes. Hot air balloons rise over the valleys at sunrise, and the frescoed churches of the Göreme Open Air Museum, Ihlara Valley and Selime Monastery can all be visited.

faqs.q: How deep are Cappadocia's underground cities?
faqs.a: Derinkuyu, the best known, is about 85 metres deep, and only about ten percent of it can be visited. Kaymaklı is carved eight levels deep, of which four are open. Both were used for centuries as places to hide from attack.

faqs.q: What is there to see in Bodrum?
faqs.a: Bodrum Castle, the Castle of St. Peter, built by the Knights Hospitaller in the 15th century and now home to the Museum of Underwater Archaeology; the site of the Mausoleum of Halicarnassus; the harbour, where gulets are still built; and the marinas at Bodrum and Yalıkavak.

faqs.q: How many UNESCO World Heritage sites does Türkiye have?
faqs.a: Twenty-two, according to UNESCO, among them the Historic Areas of Istanbul, Göreme National Park and the Rock Sites of Cappadocia, Aphrodisias, the Archaeological Site of Troy and Göbekli Tepe.

faqs.q: How do you get to the Bodrum peninsula?
faqs.a: Fly into Milas-Bodrum Airport. Maçakızı says it is about 40 km from the airport, and Six Senses Kaplankaya says the drive takes about 50 minutes, or about 10 minutes by helicopter. Maçakızı adds that İzmir and Dalaman airports are under three hours by road.
